messages:
Anya: Thinking out loud — proposing a "compact attestable envelope" (CAE) for on-prem/air-gapped upgrades. CAE = content-addressed chunks + a compact Merkle-like proof + a signed manifest header. Goal: let operators verify and partially apply updates without pulling whole images.
Matt: high level ok. how is this meaningfully different from "delta bundles" we've talked about? :thinking:
Anya: CAE focuses on two things: 1) operator UX for limited-storage nodes (inspect/verify without materializing full model) and 2) tiny chunk-possession proofs so distributor can prove a node has X subset (for staged syncs). not just diffs, more like "envelope semantics" + sparse proofs.
Jun: signatures/rotation question — if the envelope is signed, how do we handle signer rotation and revocation for already-distributed CAEs?
Zane: +1 on signer rotation complexity. we need an offline revocation path: revocation list baked into next manifest header or KMS-based CRL that operator can fetch out-of-band.
Anya: proposal: manifest header includes signer key id + issuance epoch. operators keep a small "trust bundle" locally (rotating via ops process). CAE verify will allow an explicit --trusted-keys file so air-gapped sites can manage rotation manually.
Alice: distribution channel concern: many customers still rely on physical media or disconnected registries. CAE must have a tiny "manifest-lite" extraction so you can inspect what's inside on USB without full extract.
Matt: concrete UX idea: `rbox envelope inspect --manifest-lite my-update.caeb` that prints header, chunk list (ids + sizes), and applied-variants. good for SOC review. :+1:
Anya: exactly. sample CLI: 
```
rbox pack --model my-model:v2 --envelope compact --signer=corp-kms --out=my-update.caeb
rbox verify --trusted-keys=trust.json my-update.caeb
rbox inspect --manifest-lite my-update.caeb
rbox apply --dry-run --verify-signatures --list-chunks my-update.caeb
```
Jun: about proof size — for very large models proofs can blow up. can we do probabilistic/sampled chunk proofs for performance? customer nodes would then request missing chunks only.
Zane: we should design proof verification complexity to be O(#changed_chunks) not O(model_size). maybe use chunk-level Merkle with a compact vector of changed leaves. samples OK for quick checks but final apply needs full verification.
Alice: rollback model — what does a safe rollback look like? operators hate long downtimes. any activation strategy that allows fast rollback without re-pulling?
Anya: idea: keep two envelope slots (active and candidate). apply -> stage chunks to candidate slot, verify, then atomic switch of pointer. rollback = flip back pointer. needs disk + retention window but no full re-pull.
Matt: similar to image dual-swap but CAE reduces staging disk by streaming only changed chunks. note: need GC policy for old chunks.
Jun: risk: DOS/CPU attack where a malicious CAE contains millions of small chunks to exhaust verifier. mitigations? bounded chunk count and proof-complexity caps enforced at apply-time.
Zane: also need tenant-level quotas and telemetry in Console when verify failures spike. ops -> alerting rules.
Alice: operator UX: need `inspect --show-proof-sample` and a human-friendly table, also explain why a chunk isn't present (missing, corrupted, signature mismatch).
Matt: compatibility: map CAE to our existing manifest format by adding envelope metadata keys. makes onboarding easier.
Anya: one other thought: partial-apply for constrained nodes (edge). allow a "graceful-degrade" flag that stage core weights first and optional expansions later. must be explicit in manifest.
Jun: testing/CI: we should add unit tests for verify hotpaths and a small lab harness that simulates USB distribution and offline key rotation.
Zane: ops question — how does Dedicated + Private deployments differ? Dedicated can host a verifier microservice to offload proof checks; Private/on-prem nodes may run verifier sidecar.
Alice: doc ask: need an operator playbook: preflight checks, max-chunk thresholds, rollback steps, and sample commands. assign owner? Jun + Anya?
Anya: happy to co-own. Jun can take the USB/rotation playbook bits. I'll draft RFC appendix with CLI examples.
ops-bot: Reminder: Architecture sync 2024-11-02 10:00AM scheduled (calendar link).
Matt: ok let's capture these action items in the RFC follow-up. will add a compatibility checklist and perf budget. :thumbsup:
